_comment: Who 'Ask …' can ask besides Prime itself. Used by bin/ask-ai, by the rows
bin/prime-snip-actions adds to the snip sheet and right-click menus, and by
Settings → AI Assistant, which turns rows on and off and stores the keys.
Prime's own assistant is separate and unchanged: it stays on whatever
~/.config/prime/ai.conf points at, and it is the only one allowed to change
settings. Everyone here is a read-only second opinion — they get the question
and the picture, nothing else.
Picking a row opens a terminal with a live session, so you can ask follow-ups
in it; close it when you're done.
Two kinds of provider:
'session'  a CLI that is already signed in on this computer. Opened
interactively and seeded with the question. A snip is passed as
a file path for it to read.
'model'    a model reached over the OpenAI-compatible API in base_url,
opened in ask-ai's own chat loop (--chat). Needs a key.
Keys: a provider's own 'key_file' is used when it has one, otherwise the
shared 'key_file' at the top of this file. Settings → AI Assistant writes
them (0600, in ~/.config/prime/keys/), so a key never has to live in a shell
profile. 'key_env' names an environment variable that wins over both, for
anyone who would rather keep it out of a file altogether.
'enabled': false hides a row from the pickers without deleting it, which is
what the switches in Settings write. A missing 'enabled' counts as true.
To change this list, copy it to ~/.config/prime/ask-providers.json and edit
that — yours is used instead and updates never overwrite it. Settings copies
it for you the first time you change anything. To add someone, copy a block
and give it a new key; the menus and the snip sheet pick it up with no
further change. The order here is the row order.
A provider whose CLI isn't installed, or whose key is missing, is skipped
with a plain message rather than failing oddly: `ask-ai --list` shows what is
actually set up on this computer.

claude.label: Claude
claude.via: the claude CLI, if it is signed in here
claude._note: session first; if the CLI is missing, the model is used over base_url

gemini.label: Gemini
gemini.via: the gemini CLI, if it is signed in here
gemini._note: same: the CLI when it works, otherwise the model over base_url

local.label: Local model
local.via: a model running on this computer — nothing leaves the machine
